en: He is the universe (Vishva), the all-pervading one (Vishnu), the one invoked in sacrifice (Vashatkara), the lord of past, future and present (Bhutabhavyabhavatprabhu), the maker of beings (Bhutakrit), their supporter (Bhutabhrit), pure existence (Bhava), the self of all beings (Bhutatma) and the one who brings them forth (Bhutabhavana).

first: पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः।
en: He is the pure Self (Putatma), the Supreme Self (Paramatma), the highest goal of the freed (Muktanam Parama Gati), the undying one (Avyaya), the Person (Purusha), the witness (Sakshi), the knower of the field (Kshetrajna) and the imperishable (Akshara).

He is union (Yoga), the guide of those who know yoga (Yogavidam Neta), the lord of nature and spirit (Pradhanapurusheshvara), the one in the man-lion form (Narasimhavapu), the glorious one (Shriman), the fair-haired one (Keshava) and the Supreme Person (Purushottama).

He is everything (Sarva), the destroyer (Sharva), the auspicious one (Shiva), the unmoving (Sthanu), the source of beings (Bhutadi), the undying treasure (Nidhir Avyaya), the one who appears by his own will (Sambhava), the giver of life (Bhavana), the sustainer (Bharta), the origin (Prabhava), the master (Prabhu) and the ruler (Ishvara).

He is self-born (Svayambhu), the giver of joy (Shambhu), the son of Aditi (Aditya), the lotus-eyed (Pushkaraksha), the one with a mighty voice (Mahasvana), without beginning or end (Anadinidhana), the upholder (Dhata), the arranger (Vidhata) and the highest element (Dhaturuttama).

He is beyond measure (Aprameya), the lord of the senses (Hrishikesha), lotus-navelled (Padmanabha), lord of the immortals (Amaraprabhu), maker of the universe (Vishvakarma), the thinker (Manu), the shaper (Tvashta), the most massive (Sthavishtha), the ancient (Sthavira) and the steady one (Dhruva).

He cannot be grasped (Agrahya), is eternal (Shashvata), dark and all-attracting (Krishna), red-eyed (Lohitaksha), the destroyer (Pratardana), full of all wealth (Prabhuta), the abode of the three regions (Trikakubdhama), the purifier (Pavitra) and the highest blessing (Mangalam Param).

first: ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः।
en: He is the ruler (Ishana), the giver of breath (Pranada), breath itself (Prana), the eldest (Jyeshtha), the best (Shreshtha), the lord of creatures (Prajapati), the golden womb (Hiranyagarbha), the one who holds the earth within (Bhugarbha), the husband of Lakshmi (Madhava) and the slayer of the demon Madhu (Madhusudana).

first: ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः।
en: He is the Lord (Ishvara), the valiant (Vikrami), the archer (Dhanvi), the wise (Medhavi), the one of mighty strides (Vikrama), the one who pervades (Krama), the unsurpassed (Anuttama), the one none can overcome (Duradharsha), the one who remembers good deeds (Kritajna), action itself (Kriti) and the master of himself (Atmavan).

He is lord of the gods (Suresha), the refuge (Sharana), bliss (Sharma), the seed of the universe (Vishvareta), the source of creatures (Prajabhava), the day (Aha), the year (Samvatsara), the one hard to catch, like a serpent (Vyala), trust (Pratyaya) and the one who sees all (Sarvadarshana).

He is unborn (Aja), lord of all (Sarveshvara), the perfect one (Siddha), success itself (Siddhi), the beginning of all (Sarvadi), the one who never falls (Achyuta), the lord who is dharma and Varaha (Vrishakapi), of immeasurable nature (Ameyatma) and the one reached through every path of yoga (Sarvayogavinihsrita).

He is the dweller in all (Vasu), of generous mind (Vasumana), the truth (Satya), the same to all (Samatma), beyond comparison (Asammita), even (Sama), never fruitless (Amogha), lotus-eyed (Pundarikaksha), of righteous deeds (Vrishakarma) and righteousness in form (Vrishakriti).

He is the one who makes beings weep at the end (Rudra), many-headed (Bahushira), the supporter of the worlds (Babhru), the source of the universe (Vishvayoni), of pure fame (Shuchishrava), immortal (Amrita), eternal (Shashvata), firm (Sthanu), the excellent goal (Vararoha) and of great austerity (Mahatapa).

He goes everywhere (Sarvaga), knows all (Sarvavid), is the shining one (Bhanu), whose army goes everywhere (Vishvaksena), who troubles wicked people (Janardana); he is the Veda (Veda), knower of the Veda (Vedavid), complete in all parts (Avyanga), whose limbs are the Vedic sciences (Vedanga), the one who reflects on the Veda (Vedavit) and the seer (Kavi).

He oversees the worlds (Lokadhyaksha), the gods (Suradhyaksha) and dharma (Dharmadhyaksha); he is both effect and cause (Kritakrita), fourfold in self (Chaturatma), in four forms (Chaturvyuha), four-tusked (Chaturdamshtra) and four-armed (Chaturbhuja).

He is radiant (Bhrajishnu), the food (Bhojana) and the eater (Bhokta), the patient one (Sahishnu), first-born in the world (Jagadadija), sinless (Anagha), victory (Vijaya), the conqueror (Jeta), the source of all (Vishvayoni) and the one who dwells again and again in bodies (Punarvasu).

He is the younger brother of Indra (Upendra), the dwarf (Vamana), the tall one (Pramshu), never fruitless (Amogha), pure (Shuchi), mighty (Urjita), above Indra (Atindra), the one who gathers all in (Sangraha), creation (Sarga), self-controlled (Dhritatma), the rule (Niyama) and the controller (Yama).

first: वेद्यो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः।
en: He is the one to be known (Vedya), the healer (Vaidya), ever in yoga (Sadayogi), slayer of demon heroes (Viraha), lord of knowledge (Madhava), sweet like honey (Madhu), beyond the senses (Atindriya), of great illusive power (Mahamaya), of great zeal (Mahotsaha) and of great strength (Mahabala).

He has great wisdom (Mahabuddhi), great valour (Mahavirya), great power (Mahashakti), great splendour (Mahadyuti), a form that cannot be described (Anirdeshyavapu); he is glorious (Shriman), of immeasurable nature (Ameyatma) and the bearer of the great mountain (Mahadridhrik).

He is the great archer (Maheshvasa), the supporter of the earth (Mahibharta), the dwelling of Lakshmi (Shrinivasa), the goal of the good (Satam Gati), the unstoppable (Aniruddha), the joy of the gods (Surananda), the protector of cows and finder of the earth (Govinda) and lord of those who know speech (Govidam Pati).

He is a ray of light (Marichi), the tamer (Damana), the swan (Hamsa), the fair-winged bird (Suparna), the best of serpents (Bhujagottama), golden-navelled (Hiranyanabha), of good austerity (Sutapa), lotus-navelled (Padmanabha) and lord of creatures (Prajapati).

first: अमृत्युः सर्वदृक् सिंहः सन्धाता सन्धिमान् स्थिरः।
en: He is deathless (Amrityu), all-seeing (Sarvadrik), the lion (Simha), the one who joins (Sandhata), the one who is joined (Sandhiman), firm (Sthira), unborn (Aja), unbearable to foes (Durmarshana), the teacher (Shasta), of famous nature (Vishrutatma) and slayer of the gods' enemies (Surariha).

He is the teacher (Guru), the greatest teacher (Gurutama), the abode (Dhama), the truth (Satya), of true valour (Satyaparakrama), the one who closes his eyes (Nimisha), the ever-watchful (Animisha), wearer of garlands (Sragvi), lord of speech (Vachaspati) and of noble mind (Udaradhi).

He is the leader in front (Agrani), the chief of the people (Gramani), glorious (Shriman), justice (Nyaya), the guide (Neta), the moving wind (Samirana), thousand-headed (Sahasramurdha), the soul of the universe (Vishvatma), thousand-eyed (Sahasraksha) and thousand-footed (Sahasrapat).

He turns the wheel of the world (Avartana), is a self apart from the world (Nivrittatma), is veiled (Samvrita), the crusher (Sampramardana), the day (Aha), the one who brings the world to an end (Samvartaka), fire (Vahni), wind (Anila) and the bearer of the earth (Dharanidhara).

He is very gracious (Suprasada), of joyful nature (Prasannatma), the bearer of the universe (Vishvadhrik), the enjoyer of it (Vishvabhuk), all-pervading (Vibhu), the one who honours the good (Satkarta), the one honoured (Satkrita), the good (Sadhu), the one who carries beings away (Jahnu), Narayana and Nara.

He is countless (Asankhyeya), of measureless nature (Aprameyatma), the distinguished (Vishishta), the maker of the disciplined (Shishtakrit), pure (Shuchi), the one whose aims are fulfilled (Siddhartha), whose will is fulfilled (Siddhasankalpa), the giver of success (Siddhida) and the means of success (Siddhisadhana).

He is the lord of sacred rites (Vrishahi), the bull (Vrishabha), the all-pervading (Vishnu), the one whose steps are dharma (Vrishaparva), whose belly holds dharma (Vrishodara), the one who makes grow (Vardhana), who grows (Vardhamana), the one apart (Vivikta) and the ocean of the scriptures (Shrutisagara).

first: सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः।
en: He has beautiful arms (Subhuja), is hard to hold (Durdhara), eloquent (Vagmi), the great Indra (Mahendra), the giver of wealth (Vasuda), wealth itself (Vasu), of many forms (Naikarupa), of vast form (Brihadrupa), present in the rays (Shipivishta) and the one who reveals (Prakashana).

He holds vigour, energy and brilliance (Ojastejodyutidhara), is of shining nature (Prakashatma), the one who burns (Pratapana), the prosperous (Riddha), whose words are clear (Spashtakshara), the sacred mantra (Mantra), the moonbeam (Chandramshu) and the sun's splendour (Bhaskaradyuti).

He is the source of the moon (Amritamshudbhava), the sun (Bhanu), the hare-marked moon (Shashabindu), lord of the gods (Sureshvara), the medicine (Aushadham), the bridge of the world (Jagatah Setu) and the one whose acts are true and righteous (Satyadharmaparakrama).

He is lord of past, future and present (Bhutabhavyabhavannatha), the wind (Pavana), the purifier (Pavana), fire (Anala), the slayer of desire (Kamaha), the fulfiller of desire (Kamakrit), the lovely one (Kanta), love (Kama), the giver of what is desired (Kamaprada) and the master (Prabhu).

He makes the ages begin (Yugadikrit), turns the cycle of ages (Yugavarta), has many magic powers (Naikamaya), devours all at the end (Mahashana), is invisible (Adrishya), and of visible form (Vyaktarupa); he conquers thousands (Sahasrajit) and the endless (Anantajit).

He is the beloved (Ishta), the one above difference (Avishishta), dear to the disciplined (Shishteshta), wearer of a peacock feather (Shikhandi), the one who binds (Nahusha), dharma (Vrisha), destroyer of anger (Krodhaha), the one who rouses anger against evil (Krodhakrit), the doer (Karta), the one whose arms are everywhere (Vishvabahu) and bearer of the earth (Mahidhara).

He is the one who never falls (Achyuta), the renowned (Prathita), breath (Prana), giver of breath (Pranada), younger brother of Indra (Vasavanuja), the treasure of the waters (Apamnidhi), the foundation (Adhishthana), the ever-alert (Apramatta) and the established one (Pratishthita).

He is the one who flows, like nectar (Skanda), the upholder of the right path (Skandadhara), the bearer of burdens (Dhurya), giver of boons (Varada), the one who drives the winds (Vayuvahana), the dweller in all (Vasudeva), of great light (Brihadbhanu), the first God (Adideva) and the destroyer of cities (Purandara).

He is free of sorrow (Ashoka), the one who carries across (Tarana), the saviour (Tara), the brave (Shura), the descendant of Shura (Shauri), lord of people (Janeshvara), the kindly (Anukula), the one who came a hundred times (Shatavarta), holder of the lotus (Padmi) and lotus-eyed (Padmanibhekshana).

He is lotus-navelled (Padmanabha), lotus-eyed (Aravindaksha), the one in the heart-lotus (Padmagarbha), bearer of bodies (Sharirabhrit), of great riches (Maharddhi), prosperous (Riddha), the ancient self (Vriddhatma), large-eyed (Mahaksha) and the one with Garuda on his banner (Garudadhvaja).

He is matchless (Atula), the one who dwells in bodies (Sharabha), the terrible (Bhima), the knower of right times (Samayajna), the offering (Havirhari), the one with every auspicious mark (Sarvalakshanalakshanya), with Lakshmi (Lakshmivan) and the winner of battles (Samitinjaya).

He is unfading (Vikshara), red (Rohita), the path (Marga), the cause (Hetu), the one bound with a rope at the waist (Damodara), the patient (Saha), the bearer of the earth (Mahidhara), the most fortunate (Mahabhaga), the swift (Vegavan) and the one who consumes without limit (Amitashana).

He is the origin (Udbhava), the one who stirs things up (Kshobhana), the shining God (Deva), the one who holds Lakshmi within (Shrigarbha), the Supreme Lord (Parameshvara), the instrument (Karana), the cause (Karana), the doer (Karta), the one who makes variety (Vikarta), the deep (Gahana) and the hidden (Guha).

He is resolve (Vyavasaya), the one who sets all in order (Vyavasthana), the final resting place (Samsthana), giver of position (Sthanada), the fixed (Dhruva), of supreme wealth (Pararddhi), the clearest (Paramaspashta), content (Tushta), full (Pushta) and of auspicious gaze (Shubhekshana).

first: रामो विरामो विरजो (or विरतो) मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः।
en: He is the delight (Rama), the place of rest (Virama), the stainless (Viraja), the path (Marga), the one to be led to (Neya), the guide (Naya), the one no one leads (Anaya), the hero (Vira), the best of the strong (Shaktimatam Shreshtha), dharma itself (Dharma) and the greatest knower of dharma (Dharmaviduttama).

first: वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः।
en: He is the lord of Vaikuntha (Vaikuntha), the Person (Purusha), breath (Prana), giver of breath (Pranada), the sacred syllable Om (Pranava), the vast (Prithu), the golden womb (Hiranyagarbha), slayer of enemies (Shatrughna), the all-pervading (Vyapta), the wind (Vayu) and the one beyond sense knowledge (Adhokshaja).

He is the season (Ritu), the one of pleasing sight (Sudarshana), time (Kala), the one in the highest place (Parameshthi), the one who accepts (Parigraha), the fierce (Ugra), the year (Samvatsara), the skilful (Daksha), the place of rest (Vishrama) and the most generous to all (Vishvadakshina).

He is the expanse (Vistara), the firm support of the unmoving (Sthavarasthanu), the measure of truth (Pramana), the undying seed (Bijam Avyayam), the aim (Artha), the one who needs nothing (Anartha), the great treasure-house (Mahakosha), the great enjoyment (Mahabhoga) and of great wealth (Mahadhana).

He is never weary (Anirvinna), the most massive (Sthavishtha), unborn (Abhu), the post of dharma (Dharmayupa), the great sacrifice (Mahamakha), the hub of the stars (Nakshatranemi), lord of the stars (Nakshatri), the able (Kshama), the one who remains when all wastes away (Kshama) and the one who wills (Samihana).

first: यज्ञ इज्यो महेज्यश्च क्रतुः सत्रं सतां गतिः।
en: He is the sacrifice (Yajna), the one to be worshipped (Ijya), most worthy of worship (Mahejya), the rite (Kratu), the long sacrifice (Satra), the goal of the good (Satam Gati), the all-seeing (Sarvadarshi), of free nature (Vimuktatma), all-knowing (Sarvajna) and the highest knowledge (Jnanam Uttamam).

first: सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत्।
en: He keeps good vows (Suvrata), has a lovely face (Sumukha), is subtle (Sukshma), of pleasing sound (Sughosha), giver of happiness (Sukhada), the good friend (Suhrit), charming the mind (Manohara), the conqueror of anger (Jitakrodha), of heroic arms (Virabahu) and the one who tears apart the wicked (Vidarana).

He puts beings to sleep (Svapana), depends on none (Svavasha), pervades all (Vyapi), has many selves (Naikatma), does many deeds (Naikakarmakrit), is the year (Vatsara), loving like a parent (Vatsala), the one who cares for his children (Vatsi), holds jewels within (Ratnagarbha) and is lord of wealth (Dhaneshvara).

He protects dharma (Dharmagup), practises dharma (Dharmakrit), upholds dharma (Dharmi); he is what is and what is not (Sadasat), the perishable and the imperishable (Ksharam Aksharam), the one who does not know as others know (Avijnata), thousand-rayed (Sahasramshu), the arranger (Vidhata) and the one of well-known marks (Kritalakshana).

He is the hub of the rays (Gabhastinemi), dwells in goodness (Sattvastha), is the lion (Simha), the great lord of beings (Bhutamaheshvara), the first God (Adideva), the great God (Mahadeva), lord of the gods (Devesha) and their supporter and teacher (Devabhrid Guru).

He is the one who lifts beings across (Uttara), lord of cows (Gopati), the protector (Gopta), reached by knowledge (Jnanagamya), the ancient (Puratana), supporter of the elements of the body (Sharirabhutabhrit), the enjoyer (Bhokta), lord of the monkeys (Kapindra) and the one who gives great gifts (Bhuridakshina).

He drinks the Soma (Somapa), drinks nectar (Amritapa), is the moon (Soma), conquers many (Purujit), is the best among many (Purusattama), the one who disciplines (Vinaya), victory (Jaya), true to his promise (Satyasandha), the descendant of Dasharha (Dasharha) and lord of the Satvatas (Satvatam Pati).

He is the living soul (Jiva), the guide to good conduct (Vinayita), the witness (Sakshi), the giver of freedom (Mukunda), of boundless valour (Amitavikrama), the ocean (Ambhonidhi), of endless nature (Anantatma), the one who lies on the great ocean (Mahodadhishaya) and the one who ends all (Antaka).

He is unborn (Aja), most worthy of honour (Maharha), true to his own nature (Svabhavya), conqueror of foes (Jitamitra), the giver of delight (Pramodana), bliss (Ananda), the one who delights others (Nandana), joy (Nanda), the one whose dharma is true (Satyadharma) and the one who took three great strides (Trivikrama).

He is the great sage (Maharshi), the teacher Kapila (Kapilacharya), the one who knows what was done (Kritajna), lord of the earth (Medinipati), the one of three steps (Tripada), overseer of the gods (Tridashadhyaksha), the great-horned fish (Mahashringa) and the one who ends death itself (Kritantakrit).

He is the great boar (Mahavaraha), the finder of the earth (Govinda), the one with a fine army (Sushena), wearer of golden armlets (Kanakangadi), the secret (Guhya), the deep (Gabhira), the hard to enter (Gahana), the hidden (Gupta) and the bearer of discus and mace (Chakragadadhara).

He is the creator (Vedha), his own instrument (Svanga), the unconquered (Ajita), Krishna, the firm (Dridha), the one who draws all in (Sankarshana), the one who never falls (Achyuta), Varuna, the son of Varuna (Varuna), the tree (Vriksha), lotus-eyed (Pushkaraksha) and great-minded (Mahamana).

He is the Blessed Lord (Bhagavan), the one who takes away power at the end (Bhagaha), the joyful (Anandi), wearer of the forest garland (Vanamali), the one armed with the plough (Halayudha), the son of Aditi (Aditya), the sun of light (Jyotiraditya), the patient (Sahishnu) and the best goal (Gatisattama).

He has a fine bow (Sudhanva), the axe that cuts down foes (Khandaparashu), is fierce to the wicked (Daruna), the giver of wealth (Dravinaprada), the one who touches heaven (Divahsprik), the all-seeing (Sarvadrik), the arranger of the Vedas (Vyasa), lord of speech (Vachaspati) and not born of a womb (Ayonija).

first: त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक्।
en: He is praised by the three Samans (Trisama), the singer of the Sama (Samaga), the Sama chant itself (Sama), final freedom (Nirvana), the medicine (Bheshaja), the physician (Bhishak), the one who set up the life of renunciation (Sannyasakrit), calm (Shama), peaceful (Shanta), the final ground (Nishtha), peace (Shanti) and the highest refuge (Parayana).

He has beautiful limbs (Shubhanga), gives peace (Shantida), is the creator (Srashta), the joy of the earth (Kumuda), the one who lies in the waters (Kuvaleshaya), the friend of cows (Gohita), lord of cows (Gopati), the protector (Gopta), the one whose eye is dharma (Vrishabhaksha) and the lover of dharma (Vrishapriya).

He never turns back (Anivarti), is of detached nature (Nivrittatma), the one who draws all back in (Sankshepta), maker of welfare (Kshemakrit), the auspicious (Shiva), bearer of the Shrivatsa on his chest (Shrivatsavaksha), the dwelling of Lakshmi (Shrivasa), her husband (Shripati) and the best of the glorious (Shrimatam Vara).

He gives fortune (Shrida), is lord of fortune (Shrisha), the dwelling of fortune (Shrinivasa), the treasury of fortune (Shrinidhi), the one who spreads fortune (Shrivibhavana), the holder of Lakshmi (Shridhara), the maker of fortune (Shrikara), the highest good (Shreya), the glorious (Shriman) and the refuge of the three worlds (Lokatrayashraya).

He has lovely eyes (Svaksha), lovely limbs (Svanga), a hundred joys (Shatananda), is joy (Nandi), lord of the hosts of light (Jyotirganeshvara), self-controlled (Vijitatma), ruled by no one (Avidheyatma), of true fame (Satkirti) and the remover of doubts (Chhinnasamshaya).

He is exalted (Udirna), has eyes on all sides (Sarvatashchakshu), has no lord above him (Anisha), is eternal and steady (Shashvatasthira), the one who lay on the ground (Bhushaya), the adornment of the earth (Bhushana), prosperity (Bhuti), free of sorrow (Vishoka) and the destroyer of sorrow (Shokanashana).

He is radiant (Archishman), the one worshipped (Archita), the vessel that holds all (Kumbha), of pure nature (Vishuddhatma), the purifier (Vishodhana), the unstoppable (Aniruddha), the one without a rival (Apratiratha), the one of great wealth (Pradyumna) and of boundless valour (Amitavikrama).

He is the slayer of the demon Kalanemi (Kalaneminiha), the hero (Vira), the descendant of Shura (Shauri), lord of the brave (Shurajaneshvara), the self of the three worlds (Trilokatma), lord of the three worlds (Trilokesha), the long-haired one (Keshava), slayer of the demon Keshi (Keshiha) and the remover of sin (Hari).

He is the god of love (Kamadeva), the guardian of desires (Kamapala), the one who has all desires fulfilled (Kami), the lovely (Kanta), the giver of scriptures (Kritagama), of indescribable form (Anirdeshyavapu), the all-pervading (Vishnu), the hero (Vira), the endless (Ananta) and the winner of wealth (Dhananjaya).

He is devoted to Brahman (Brahmanya), the maker of the Vedas and of austerity (Brahmakrit), the creator Brahma, Brahman itself, the one who makes the Vedas grow (Brahmavivardhana), the knower of Brahman (Brahmavid), the Brahmin (Brahmana), the one who has Brahman (Brahmi), the knower of the Vedas (Brahmajna) and dear to Brahmins (Brahmanapriya).

He takes great steps (Mahakrama), does great deeds (Mahakarma), has great brilliance (Mahateja), is the great serpent (Mahoraga), the great rite (Mahakratu), the great sacrificer (Mahayajva), the great sacrifice (Mahayajna) and the great offering (Mahahavi).

first: स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः।
en: He is worthy of praise (Stavya), fond of praise (Stavapriya), the hymn (Stotra), the act of praise (Stuti), the one who praises (Stota), fond of battle (Ranapriya), full (Purna), the one who fills (Purayita), holy (Punya), of holy fame (Punyakirti) and free of disease (Anamaya).

He is swift as the mind (Manojava), the maker of holy places and teachings (Tirthakara), whose seed is golden (Vasureta), the giver of wealth (Vasuprada), again the giver of wealth (Vasuprada), the son of Vasudeva (Vasudeva), the dweller in all (Vasu), of generous mind (Vasumana) and the offering (Havi).

He is the goal of the good (Sadgati), good action (Satkriti), being itself (Satta), true glory (Sadbhuti), the highest goal of the good (Satparayana), the one whose army is brave (Shurasena), the best of the Yadus (Yadushreshtha), the dwelling of the good (Sannivasa) and the one of the Yamuna banks (Suyamuna).

He is the dwelling of beings (Bhutavasa), the god who dwells in all (Vasudeva), the resting place of all lives (Sarvasunilaya), fire that is never enough (Anala), destroyer of pride (Darpaha), giver of pride in dharma (Darpada), the joyful (Dripta), hard to hold (Durdhara) and the unconquered (Aparajita).

He is the universe as his form (Vishvamurti), of great form (Mahamurti), of blazing form (Diptamurti), without form (Amurtiman), of many forms (Anekamurti), unmanifest (Avyakta), of a hundred forms (Shatamurti) and of a hundred faces (Shatanana).

first: एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत् तत्पदमनुत्तमम्।
en: He is the One (Eka), the many (Naika), the Soma rite (Sava), bliss (Ka), the one asked about (Kim), the one from whom all comes (Yat), That (Tat), the highest state (Padam Anuttamam), the kinsman of the world (Lokabandhu), lord of the world (Lokanatha), lord of Lakshmi (Madhava) and the one who loves his devotees (Bhaktavatsala).

He is golden in colour (Suvarnavarna), with a golden body (Hemanga), of fine limbs (Varanga), wearing sandal paste and armlets (Chandanangadi), slayer of demon heroes (Viraha), the unequalled (Vishama), the void (Shunya), the one who needs no blessings (Ghritashi), the unmoving (Achala) and the moving (Chala).

He is free of pride (Amani), the giver of honour (Manada), the one to be honoured (Manya), master of the world (Lokasvami), bearer of the three worlds (Trilokadhrik), of fine intelligence (Sumedha), born of the sacrifice (Medhaja), blessed (Dhanya), of true intelligence (Satyamedha) and bearer of the earth (Dharadhara).

He showers brilliance (Tejovrisha), holds splendour (Dyutidhara), is the best of all who bear weapons (Sarvashastrabhritam Vara), the one who accepts offerings (Pragraha), the one who restrains (Nigraha), the one never at a loss (Vyagra), the many-horned one (Naikashringa) and the elder brother of Gada (Gadagraja).

He has four forms (Chaturmurti), four arms (Chaturbahu), four manifestations (Chaturvyuha), is the goal of the four orders of life (Chaturgati), fourfold in self (Chaturatma), the source of the four aims of life (Chaturbhava), the knower of the four Vedas (Chaturvedavid) and the one of whom a single part is the world (Ekapat).

He turns the wheel of life (Samavarta), never turns away (Anivrittatma), is hard to conquer (Durjaya), hard to go beyond (Duratikrama), hard to reach (Durlabha), hard to approach (Durgama), hard to attain (Durga), hard to make his dwelling (Duravasa) and the slayer of evil foes (Durariha).

He has fair limbs (Shubhanga), takes the essence of the world (Lokasaranga), is the fine thread (Sutantu), the one who extends the thread of the world (Tantuvardhana), whose deeds are like Indra's (Indrakarma), of great deeds (Mahakarma), whose work is done (Kritakarma) and the author of the scriptures (Kritagama).

He is the source (Udbhava), the beautiful (Sundara), the compassionate (Sunda), jewel-navelled (Ratnanabha), of lovely eyes (Sulochana), the sun (Arka), the giver of food (Vajasana), the horned one (Shringi), the victor (Jayanta), the all-knowing (Sarvavit) and the one who always wins (Jayi).

He has golden limbs (Suvarnabindu), is unshakeable (Akshobhya), the lord of all lords of speech (Sarvavagishvareshvara), the great lake (Mahahrada), the great abyss (Mahagarta), the great Being (Mahabhuta) and the great treasure (Mahanidhi).

He is the joy of the earth (Kumuda), the giver of the earth (Kundara), as pure as jasmine (Kunda), the rain cloud (Parjanya), the purifier (Pavana), the wind (Anila), the source of nectar (Amritamsha), of immortal body (Amritavapu), all-knowing (Sarvajna) and with faces on every side (Sarvatomukha).

He is easy to reach (Sulabha), keeps fine vows (Suvrata), is perfect (Siddha), conquers enemies (Shatrujit), burns enemies (Shatrutapana), is the banyan, the fig and the holy fig tree (Nyagrodha, Udumbara, Ashvattha) and the slayer of Chanura of Andhra (Chanurandhranishudana).

He has a thousand flames (Sahasrarchi), seven tongues (Saptajihva), seven fires (Saptaidha), seven horses (Saptavahana); he is formless (Amurti), sinless (Anagha), beyond thought (Achintya), the one who causes fear to the wicked (Bhayakrit) and the destroyer of fear (Bhayanashana).

He is tiny (Anu), vast (Brihat), thin (Krisha), large (Sthula), the bearer of qualities (Gunabhrit), free of qualities (Nirguna), great (Mahan), held up by nothing (Adhrita), self-supported (Svadhrita), of fine face (Svasya), of the first family (Pragvamsha) and the one who makes families grow (Vamshavardhana).

He bears the burden of the world (Bharabhrit), is the one spoken of in scripture (Kathita), the yogi (Yogi), lord of yogis (Yogisha), giver of all desires (Sarvakamada), the place of rest (Ashrama), the one who troubles the worldly (Shramana), the one who wastes away all at the end (Kshama), the fair-winged bird (Suparna) and the mover of the winds (Vayuvahana).

He bears the bow (Dhanurdhara), is the science of archery (Dhanurveda), the rod of law (Danda), the one who tames (Damayita), self-restraint (Dama), the unconquered (Aparajita), the one who bears all (Sarvasaha), the controller (Niyanta), free of rules (Aniyama) and free of death's control (Ayama).

He is full of goodness (Sattvavan), pure in nature (Sattvika), the truth (Satya), devoted to truth and dharma (Satyadharmaparayana), the one sought by all (Abhipraya), worthy of love (Priyarha), worthy (Arha), the one who does what pleases (Priyakrit) and the one who increases joy (Pritivardhana).

He moves through the sky (Vihayasagati), is light (Jyoti), of lovely radiance (Suruchi), the fire that eats the offerings (Hutabhuk), the all-pervading (Vibhu), the sun (Ravi), the shining one (Virochana), the sun (Surya), the begetter (Savita) and the one whose eye is the sun (Ravilochana).

He is endless (Ananta), the eater of offerings (Hutabhuk), the enjoyer (Bhokta), the giver of happiness (Sukhada), born many times (Naikaja), the first-born (Agraja), never weary (Anirvinna), always patient (Sadamarshi), the support of the world (Lokadhishthana) and the wonderful (Adbhuta).

He is the ancient (Sanat), the most ancient (Sanatanatama), the tawny sage (Kapila), the sun (Kapi), the undying (Avyaya), the giver of welfare (Svastida), the maker of welfare (Svastikrit), welfare itself (Svasti), the enjoyer of welfare (Svastibhuk) and the one skilled in giving welfare (Svastidakshina).

He is not fierce (Araudra), wears earrings (Kundali), holds the discus (Chakri), is the valiant (Vikrami), of mighty command (Urjitashasana), beyond words (Shabdatiga), the one who bears all words (Shabdasaha), cool (Shishira) and the maker of night (Sharvarikara).

He is not cruel (Akrura), gentle (Peshala), skilful (Daksha), generous (Dakshina), the best of the patient (Kshaminam Vara), the wisest (Vidvattama), free of fear (Vitabhaya) and the one whose story is holy to hear and sing (Punyashravanakirtana).

He lifts beings across (Uttarana), destroys evil deeds (Dushkritiha), is holy (Punya), the destroyer of bad dreams (Duhsvapnanashana), slayer of demon heroes (Viraha), the protector (Rakshana), the good (Santa), life (Jivana) and the one present everywhere (Paryavasthita).

He has endless forms (Anantarupa), endless glory (Anantashri), has conquered anger (Jitamanyu), removes fear (Bhayapaha), is the just one (Chaturashra), of deep nature (Gabhiratma), the one who gives various gifts (Vidisha), the one who gives commands (Vyadisha) and the one who directs (Disha).

He has no beginning (Anadi), is the earth (Bhu), the support of the earth (Bhuva), Lakshmi (Lakshmi), the fine hero (Suvira), wearer of beautiful armlets (Ruchirangada), the begetter (Janana), the first cause of the birth of beings (Janajanmadi), the terrible (Bhima) and of terrible valour (Bhimaparakrama).

He is the abode of the supports (Adharanilaya), has no maker (Adhata), smiles like a flower (Pushpahasa), is ever wakeful (Prajagara), goes upward (Urdhvaga), walks the good path (Satpathachara), gives life (Pranada), is the syllable Om (Pranava) and the one who rewards deeds (Pana).

He is the measure of truth (Pramana), the home of breath (Prananilaya), the sustainer of breath (Pranabhrit), the life of breath (Pranajivana), the reality (Tattva), the knower of reality (Tattvavid), the one Self (Ekatma) and the one beyond birth, death and old age (Janmamrityujaratiga).

He is the tree of the three worlds (Bhurbhuvahsvastaru), the saviour (Tara), the begetter (Savita), the great-grandfather (Prapitamaha), the sacrifice (Yajna), lord of sacrifice (Yajnapati), the sacrificer (Yajva), whose limbs are the sacrifice (Yajnanga) and the one who carries the sacrifice (Yajnavahana).

He upholds the sacrifice (Yajnabhrit), makes the sacrifice (Yajnakrit), owns the sacrifice (Yajni), enjoys the sacrifice (Yajnabhuk), is the means of sacrifice (Yajnasadhana), completes the sacrifice (Yajnantakrit), the secret of sacrifice (Yajnaguhya), the food (Anna) and the eater of food (Annada).

He is his own source (Atmayoni), self-born (Svayamjata), the one who dug the earth (Vaikhana), the singer of the Sama (Samagayana), the delight of Devaki (Devakinandana), the creator (Srashta), lord of the earth (Kshitisha) and the destroyer of sin (Papanashana).

He holds the conch (Shankhabhrit), the sword Nandaka (Nandaki), the discus (Chakri), the bow Sharnga (Sharngadhanva) and the mace (Gadadhara); he has the wheel in his hand (Rathangapani), is unshakeable (Akshobhya) and has every kind of weapon (Sarvapraharanayudha).

'He who has every kind of weapon: Om, salutation to him.' May the glorious Narayana, Vishnu, Vasudeva, who wears the forest garland and holds the mace, the bow Sharnga, the conch, the discus and the sword Nandaka, protect us.
'May the glorious Vasudeva protect us: Om, salutation to him.'
